newsitem.title: USA: Union assails Boeing maintenance venture in China.
newsitem.headline: Union assails Boeing maintenance venture in China.

text.p: Boeing Co.'s biggest union Tuesday harshly criticised the company's decision to join a Chinese aircraft maintenance venture, saying it would result in the loss of U.S. jobs.

The Machinists union, which represents some 34,000 Boeing workers, said the company failed to consult with the union as required before it announced Monday that it invested $11 million for a 9.1 percent stake in Taikoo (Xiamen) Aircraft Engineering Co. Ltd.

Boeing said it had discussed the deal in advance with both local and national union leadership but was not bound by a contractual requirement to give notice 90 days in advance because the deal would not eliminate 50 or In a blistering statement, International Association of Machinists President R. Thomas Buffenbarger charged the deal would transfer "to an enslaved work force in China" future work converting Boeing 747 jets for all-cargo use, normally done at Boeing's Wichita, Kan., facility.
"It is another flagrant expression of unbridled corporate greed at the expense of the job security of American working families," Buffenbarger said.
But Boeing said the Chinese venture, known as TAECO, will bring new work to the company and will not result in the loss of any union jobs.

"We think quite strongly that we are creating jobs for our Boeing employees here in the United States, particularly in Wichita," Boeing Enterprises President Larry Clarkson said in a statement. "Additionally, we believe the growing market for new airplanes in China will create even more U.S. jobs, as it has for the last several years."
Separately, Boeing said the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service plans to buy 45 MD 600N helicopters
Separately, Boeing said the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service plans to buy 45 MD 600N helicopters with a total value, including aircraft, spares and support, of an estimated $70.7 million.
The company said the order amounts to an agency endorsement of advanced technology helicopters over conventional rotorcraft.
The MD 600Ns will be assigned to the U.S. Border Patrol operating sectors between San Diego, Calif., and Miami, Fla., as replacement aircraft for its fleet of OH-6A helicopters, Boeing said.

Boeing said the contract award is the largest commercial helicopter order in more than 20 years for its helicopter subsidiary in Mesa, Ariz., which also produces MD 500 Series and MD Explorer helicopters.
The award calls for delivery of nine MD 600N helicopters the first year and options for nine more MD 600Ns each year for four additional years. First delivery will be in early 1998, the company said.
